But if you're offering sandwiches to people who aren't hungry, your sales will struggle. That's demand. It's pretty simple. More demand makes selling easier. Now, let's add the supply part. You send an email to your list saying that you're thinking about organizing a seminar with a well-known speaker on a certain day. And even if you think your business has no limits at all, think about your market size. Everything has a limit. When you go beyond your capacity, your quality drops and people don't get the experience they were promised. Your capacity should take into account everything that needs to happen to give your customers a great experience and help them get results with your product. If your business can truly take amazing care of just 20 clients per year, then just say it openly. It's not just about delivering the product or service. It's about giving your customers an unforgettable experience. That way, they'll talk about you to others, and your marketing budget can drop to almost zero. Traditional marketing, on the other hand ironically, favors the competition. You see an ad and realize you need that product. But what do you do? You don't just buy it from the ad. The buildup phase follows this idea. It creates a path where you show your market what's coming and collect feedback before asking them to commit and buy. In this phase, you need to have a bunch of digital content ready to share with your prospects to grab their attention, educate them, and entertain them.
